findings.excerpt: apply add_right_cancel (b := FirstHurewicz.inducedChain (lowerSection f 0) n b.1)
findings.problem: This re-proves the telescoping argument already stated as sum_range_shift_of_endpoints_mo1973_27356 (lines 934–941), which is declared earlier in the same file. Both proofs cancel the term F 0 on the right, then use Finset.sum_range_succ' and Finset.sum_range_succ, then use the periodicity hypothesis F m = F 0. Here F k = inducedChain (lowerSection f k) n b.1, and the hypothesis comes from lowerSection_period. The only difference is the instantiation of F.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the body with an application of the existing helper:
  sum_range_shift_of_endpoints_mo1973_27356 (fun k => FirstHurewicz.inducedChain (lowerSection f k) n b.1) m (by simp only [lowerSection_period f m hf])
If simp does not close the goal, use `congrArg (fun s => FirstHurewicz.inducedChain s n b.1) (lowerSection_period f m hf)`. Both lemmas are private to the same namespace, so no import changes are needed. Better still, rename the helper to a descriptive name (for example `sum_range_succ_eq_of_endpoint_eq`) and drop the `_mo1973_27356` suffix. Use it in homologyNorm_symm and in this lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicated 8-line calc, leaves one place where the telescoping-sum argument is maintained, and makes it clear that the chain-level shift and the homology-level shift are the same fact.

findings.problem: The two theorems have identical proofs and differ only by u/v renaming. Each proof forms `congrArg (fun F => inducedChain F (n+1) (crossProductEdge unitInterval X n (pathChain Path.id) b))` on a map equation. It then runs the same `simp only [inducedChain_comp, LinearMap.comp_apply, crossProductEdge_natural, inducedChain_id, LinearMap.id_apply, ...CircleMap_pathChain] at h`, and ends with `exact h.symm`. The underlying naturality reasoning is repeated, and the preceding pairs productCover_uCircleMap/vCircleMap and uCircleMap_pathChain/vCircleMap_pathChain also mirror each other.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma, for a map g : C(unitInterval, Circle), a strip s : C(unitInterval × X, Y), an inclusion ι : C(Y, Torus B.symm), and a chain c : Chains Circle 1. Assume hmap : (productCover m B hB).comp (g.prodMap (ContinuousMap.id X)) = ι.comp s, and hc : inducedChain g 1 (pathChain Path.id) = c. The conclusion is inducedChain ι (n+1) (inducedChain s (n+1) (crossProductEdge unitInterval X n (pathChain Path.id) b)) = inducedChain (productCover m B hB) (n+1) (crossProductEdge Circle X n c b). The proof is the common congrArg/simp/symm argument, with hc used in place of uCircleMap_pathChain. Then uStrip_inclusion_crossProduct is the lemma applied to productCover_uCircleMap and uCircleMap_pathChain, and the v version is the same with v in place of u. The exact implicit arguments of crossProductEdge_natural were not inspected.
findings.benefit: The naturality argument is stated and maintained once, and the u and v theorems shrink to one-line instantiations. The final sum step (line 1332) then visibly uses the same mechanism for both pieces.

findings.problem: The two boundary computations are the same argument. Each unfolds the cross chain and rewrites with inducedChain_boundary, crossProductEdge_path_boundary and map_sub. Each then splits with `congr 1` and closes both endpoint goals with the same `congrArg (fun g => inducedChain g n b.1)` plus `simpa only [inducedChain_comp, LinearMap.comp_apply]` pattern, applied to the strip_one and strip_zero equations. Only the strip, the inclusion into the intersection, and the endpoint sections differ.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma for any space Y, a strip s : C(unitInterval × X, Y), an intersection map ι : C(Z, Y), and sections a0 a1 : C(X, Z). Assume h0 : s.comp (crossInsertLeft 0) = ι.comp a0 and h1 : s.comp (crossInsertLeft 1) = ι.comp a1. The conclusion is that ((singularComplex Y).d (n+1) n).hom (inducedChain s (n+1) (crossProductEdge unitInterval X n (pathChain Path.id) b.1)) = inducedChain ι n (inducedChain a1 n b.1 - inducedChain a0 n b.1). The proof is the shared rw/congr/simpa block. Then uCrossChain_boundary follows from uStrip_one and uStrip_zero, and vCrossChain_boundary from vStrip_one and vStrip_zero, with a1 = lowerSection f (k+1) and a0 = upperSection f k in the v case. Exact argument names depend on crossInsertLeft and the Cycle coercions.
findings.benefit: One lemma carries the chain-level boundary computation, so the u and v statements, which differ only in which sections appear, are visibly parallel. The nontrivial rewrite is no longer maintained twice.
